verses.1:1: The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord God says to Idumea—I have heard a report from the Lord, and He has sent out a siege to the nations: "Rise up, and let us rise up against her for war!"
verses.1:2: "Look, I have made you very small among the nations; you are greatly dishonored.
verses.1:3: The arrogance of your heart has lifted you up, you who dwell in the crevices of the rocks; raising his dwelling high, saying in his heart, 'Who will bring me down to the ground?'
verses.1:4: If you soar high like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down," says the Lord.
verses.1:5: "If thieves had come in to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? Would they not have stolen what was enough for themselves? And if grape-gatherers had come in to you, would they not have left behind gleanings?
verses.1:6: How Esau has been searched out, and his hidden things have been seized!
verses.1:7: As far as the borders they have sent you out; all the men of your covenant have stood against you; men at peace with you have prevailed against you; they have set ambushes under you; there is no understanding in them.
verses.1:8: In that day," says the Lord, "I will destroy wise men from Idumea and understanding from Mount Esau.
verses.1:9: And your warriors from Teman will be terrified, so that man may be removed from Mount Esau.
verses.1:10: Because of the slaughter and the ungodliness against your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.
verses.1:11: From the day you stood opposite, in the days when foreigners were taking his force captive, and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
verses.1:12: And do not look upon the day of your brother in the day of strangers, and do not rejoice over the sons of Judah in the day of their destruction, and do not speak boastfully in the day of distress.
verses.1:13: And do not enter the gates of peoples in the day of their hardships, nor should you also look upon their assembly in the day of their ruin, nor join in attacking their force in the day of their destruction.
verses.1:14: And do not stand at his passes to utterly destroy his survivors, nor shut in his fugitives in the day of distress.
verses.1:15: For the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations; just as you have done, so it will be to you; your repayment will be repaid upon your head.
verses.1:16: For just as you drank upon My holy mountain, they will drink and go down, and they will be as though they did not exist.
verses.1:17: But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy, and the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.
verses.1:18: And the house of Jacob will be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; and they will be kindled against them and devour them, and there will be no fire-bearer for the house of Esau," for the Lord has spoken.
verses.1:19: And those in the Negev will possess Mount Esau, and those in the Shephelah, the foreigners; and they will possess Mount Ephraim and the plain of Samaria and Benjamin and Gilead.
verses.1:20: And this is the beginning of the exile: for the sons of Israel, the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exile of Jerusalem as far as Ephrathah; they will inherit the cities of the Negev.
verses.1:21: And survivors will go up from Mount Zion to take vengeance on Mount Esau, and the kingdom will belong to the Lord.

notes.1:1: The Greek uses the name Idumea (for Hebrew Edom) and reads "a siege" (Greek perioche, also "blockade"), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew word for "envoy" as related to besieging.
notes.1:13: The Greek reads plural "peoples" (where the Hebrew has "My people") and "their assembly" (Greek synagogen, where the Hebrew has "his calamity").
notes.1:18: The Greek reads "fire-bearer" (Greek pyrophoros), an idiom for even a sole survivor that continues the fire imagery, where the Hebrew reads "survivor."
notes.1:20: The Greek reads "the beginning" (Greek arche, which can also mean "domain") for a difficult Hebrew phrase meaning "this host," and reads the place name "Ephrathah" where the Hebrew has "Sepharad."
notes.1:21: The Greek reads the passive participle "survivors" (literally "those who are rescued," where the Hebrew has active "deliverers"), "from Mount Zion" (Hebrew: "to Mount Zion"), and "to take vengeance on" (Hebrew: "to judge").
